claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has an approximately 71% L12 and 29% B2 lamellar dual-phase microstructure.
The B2 lamellae are approximately 2–3 µm thick and contain nanoscale Cr-rich precipitates.
The fine L12/B2 lamellar microstructure is retained after three rapid heating/quenching cycles to approximately 1100 °C.
The retained lamellar microstructure provides homogeneous or uniform Cr availability.
Uniform Cr availability promotes robust passive-film repair.
Robust passive-film repair minimizes abrasive damage and debris-induced degradation.
Temperature modulates the competition between sliding-induced depassivation and thermally activated repassivation.
At approximately 50 °C, enhanced passive-film restoration produces a stable, low-shear tribolayer and a polishing-wear regime.
At approximately 25 °C, slower passive-film repair promotes aggressive two-body abrasion.
At approximately 100 °C, unstable or intermittently rupturing oxide and tribolayer films promote third-body or oxidative wear.
The stable lamellar structure suppresses catastrophic degradation in the HEA.
The HEA outperforms duplex stainless steel 2205 under the proposed tribocorrosion conditions.
Relative to DS2205, the HEA will have a smaller and more stable wear track.
Relative to DS2205, the HEA will have lower wear volume, lower coefficient of friction, and a substantially lower tribocorrosion wear rate.
The HEA's most favorable tribocorrosion performance will occur near 50 °C.
Total degradation will increase at 25 °C and 100 °C relative to 50 °C because passive-film behavior is less effective at those temperatures.
Even at 25 °C and 100 °C, degradation of the HEA will remain milder than degradation of DS2205.
The proposed mechanism applies specifically in deionized water over 25–100 °C, 5–15 N, and 3–9 Hz using an alumina counter-body.
The proposed mechanism does not claim applicability to continuous 1100 °C service or chloride-, sulfate-, and other ion-containing environments.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says the mechanism explains accelerated wear–corrosion relative to a matched baseline, but the specified primary baseline is DS2205 and the mechanism and predicted outcome instead claim that the HEA outperforms DS2205 with lower degradation. The reference relative to which degradation is 'accelerated' is therefore internally inconsistent.

The mechanism is explicitly bounded to low-ionic-strength deionized water and excludes chloride-containing environments, yet potentiodynamic polarization in 3.5 wt.% NaCl is included among the falsification measurements. That measurement does not directly test the stated environmental boundary unless it is clearly designated as ancillary.
